IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: The implicit construction in mدهامتان supplies a subject, while al-Fajr implies an oath verb, as in I swear by the dawn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: فقولي ولو تقديرا لإدخال قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v1p251/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.claim: The debt verse is longest at 128 words and 540 letters; al-Duha then al-Fajr are shortest. He rejects مدهامتان and ثم نظر as shorter candidates based on their letter or word counts.
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.anchor: وأطول آية فيه آية الدين مائة وثمانية وعشرون كلمة وخمسمائة وأربعون حرفا

BURHAN:v1p267/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p267/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
BURHAN:v1p267/r5.claim: Abu Amr al-Dani says مدهامتان in al-Rahman is the only word that is itself a verse.
BURHAN:v1p267/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو الدانى لا أعلم كلمة هى وحدها آية إلا قوله ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾ فى سورة الرحمن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.claim: The sūrah distinguishes the characteristics of Paradise for the muqarrabīn from those for the asḥāb al-yamīn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r5.anchor: the muqarrabīn shall receive are delineated, followed by the features and characteristics of the Paradise which the asḥāb al-yamīn will be blessed with

JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r7.claim: Dahma means blackness; crops are called idhāmmat when moisture makes them dark, and the word also names a calamity, its diminutive, and a cooking pot.
JISHUMI:v9p6732#2/r7.anchor: الدهمة: السواد، وادهام الزرع: إذا علاه السواد ريا، ومنه الدهماء: الداهية

TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r1.claim: The author says two transmitted glosses support his preceding interpretation of the two images, though their precise contextual fit is left unclear below.
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r1.anchor: أقول والروايتان تؤيدان ما قدمناه في تفسير الآيتين

TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh report through Abu Ayyub that the Prophet glossed mudhammatan as green.
TABATABAI:55:31-78#2/r2.anchor: أخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عن أبي أيوب قال سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن قوله { مدهامتان } قال

NAHHAS:v4p315/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p315/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v4p315/r8.claim: Abu Hatim allows مدهمتان in ordinary speech, since both ادهم and ادهام are used.
NAHHAS:v4p315/r8.anchor: قال أبو حاتم ويجوز في الكلام مدهمتان لأنه يقال ادهم وادهام

ZAJJAJ:v5p103/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p103/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p103/r4.claim: The gardens are deeply green, tending toward black; this is the fullness and freshness of green plants.
ZAJJAJ:v5p103/r4.anchor: يعني أنهما خضراوان تضرب خضرتهما إلى السواد، وكل نبت أخضر فتمام خضرته وريه أن يضرب إلى السواد.

ASAD-NOTES:55:62/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:62/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:62/r2.claim: The two gardens are of the deepest green.

ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r1.claim: The deep green describes abundant watering, according to Taj al-'Arus.
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r1.anchor: by reason of abundant watering (Taj al-'Arus)

ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r2.claim: Green often signifies ever-fresh life in Qur'anic imagery, including paradise garments and meadows.
ASAD-NOTES:55:62#n29/r2.anchor: is often used in the Qur'an to indicate ever-fresh life

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p976/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p976/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p976/r3.claim: The Qur'an's challenge is set at surah length because an individual verse can be one word; even the short Kawthar and Ikhlas are inimitable, so Qur'anic speech of that length is miraculous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p976/r3.anchor: لم يتحداهم بآية لأن الآية قد تكون كلمة (ألم) و (مدهامتان) آية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p266/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p266/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p266/r1.claim: Qatāda describes the two gardens as lush and fresh from abundant water; when the greenery thickens, it darkens toward black.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p266/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾ قال خضراوان من الري ناعمتان إذا اشتدت الخضرة ضربتا إلى السواد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r1.claim: The dual adjective modifies the two gardens; alternatively, it predicates an omitted subject, ‘they are intensely green.’
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r1.anchor: صفة لجنتان وسط بينها الأعتراض لما تقدم من التنبيه على أن تكذيب كل من الموصوف والصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r2.claim: The interruption between the gardens and their description underscores that denying either the described thing or its attribute merits censure.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r2.anchor: التنبيه على أن تكذيب كل من الموصوف والصفة حيقي بالإنكار والتوبيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r3.claim: Duhma originally denotes the blackness of night and can describe a black horse; by proximity of color it can also denote fully saturated green.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r3.anchor: من الدهمة وهي في الأصل على ما قال الراغب سواد الليل ويعبر بها عن سواد الفرس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r4.claim: The form ادهام can mean becoming black or becoming intensely green; these gardens are very deep green, shading toward black.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r4.anchor: على وزن مفعال إذا اسود أو اشتدت خضرته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن أبي رباح
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r5.claim: These authorities and others explain مدهامتان as intensely green; a report from Abu Ayyub says the Prophet answered that the gardens are green.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r5.anchor: وفسرها هنا ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن أبي رباح وجماعة بخضراوان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي أيوب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r6.claim: Asked by Abu Ayyub about مدهامتان, the Prophet replied that the two gardens are green, meaning intensely green.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r6.anchor: سألت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير وأبو صالح
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r7.claim: They explain the dark cast of the intense green as resulting from the gardens being well watered.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r7.anchor: من الري من الماء كما روي عن ابن عباس وابن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r8.claim: The description suggests these gardens are dominated by ground-covering plants and blossoms, while the earlier gardens’ many branches suggests trees dominate there.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r8.anchor: الغالب عليهما النبات والرياحين المنبسطة على وجه الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r9.claim: On that contrast, the present pair rank below the earlier pair, since gardens rich in shade and fruit exceed gardens with less shade and fruit.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r9.anchor: في المنزلة والقدر كيف لاوالجنة الكثيرة الظلال والثمار أعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r10.claim: Those preferring the present gardens argue that greenery is especially praised in gardens and signals abundant water, care, and protection from withering.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p121#2/r10.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى تفضيل هاتين الجنتين مع اختصاص الوصف بالخضرة بالنبات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p457/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p457/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p457/r1.claim: The gardens are lush and dark green from abundant moisture; intense greenness tends toward black. The term derives from a verb for crops turning dark.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p457/r1.anchor: ناعمتان سوداوان من ريهما وشدة خضرتهما، لأن الخضرة إذا اشتدت ضربت إلى السواد، يقال: ادهام الزرع إذا علاه السواد ريا

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:63-70/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:63-70/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:63-70/r1.claim: The gardens are green tending to black from intense greenery; ground-covering plants dominate, unlike the first pair's trees and fruit, showing relative rank.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:63-70/r1.anchor: خضراوان تضربان إلى السواد من شدة الخضرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r13.claim: The two gardens are intensely green, their lushness darkening toward black because of abundant moisture; the word derives from ‘darkness.’
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r13.anchor: أي خضراوان خضرة تضرب من شدة الري إلى السواد , من الدهمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r14.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r14.claim: Al-Asbahani says these gardens are dominated by ground-covering plants and herbs, unlike the earlier pair, which has trees and fruit.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p395/r14.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : الغالب على هاتين الجنتين النبات والرياحين المنبسطة على وجه الأرض

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the two gardens as green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضروان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that abundant water made the greenery so intense that it turned dark.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r3.anchor: قد اسودتا من الخضرة التي من الري من الماء

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr describes them as green from abundant moisture.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان من الري

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r5.claim: Asked about the word, the Prophet explained that the gardens are green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r5.anchor: عن أبي أيوب قال: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r6.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r6.claim: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī says the phrase describes two green gardens.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r6.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: هما جنتان خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r7.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ glosses the gardens as green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r7.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: هما جنتان خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r8.claim: Mujāhid glosses the gardens as green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses the gardens as green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r10.claim: ʿIkrima glosses the gardens as green.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r11.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r11.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says they are green from abundant water and moist; intense greenness tends toward black.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r11.anchor: عن أبي صالح {مدهامتان} قال: خضراوان من الري ناعمتان إذا اشتدت الخضرة ضربت إلى السواد

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r12.claim: Mujāhid also glosses مدهامتان as darkened or black.

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r13.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r13.claim: Mujāhid and ʿIkrima say the gardens are black from abundant moisture.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة {مدهامتان} قالا: سوداوان من الري

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r14.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r14.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes them as black from abundant moisture.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r14.anchor: عن الضحاك {مدهامتان} قال: سوداوان من الري

DURR-FULL:v7p715/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r15.speaker: جابر بن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r15.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd recited مدهامتان and then bowed.
DURR-FULL:v7p715/r15.anchor: عن جابر بن زيد أنه قرأ {مدهامتان} ثم ركع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r1.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas, including one through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, gloss the two gardens as green.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس مدهامتان قال : خضراوان .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas describes them as nearly black from the lush greenery caused by abundant water.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3327#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : مدهامتان قال : قد اسودتا من الخضرة التي من الري من الماء .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p234#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p234#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p234#2/r11.claim: Mud'hāmmatān means intensely dark green from abundant blessing; the first two gardens have branches, but every garden has branches even if it is not so verdant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p234#2/r11.anchor: وجعل هاتين مدهامتين من شدة النعمة، والأوليين ذواتي أفنان، وكل جنة ذات أفنان وإن لم تكن مدهامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p235/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p235/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr glossed mudhāmmatān as gardens whose lush green has become intensely dark; the cited phrase in 87:5 offers a parallel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p235/r3.anchor: كذا فسره ابن الزبير على المنبر، ومنه قوله تعالى: الذي أخرج المرعى فجعله غثاء أحوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr say the two gardens are green from being well-watered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن الزبير خضراوان من الري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says their greenery has become nearly black from its intensity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة من خضرتهما قد اسودتا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reconciles the descriptions: they are green tinged with black, the full freshness of vegetation shading toward black.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p124#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج يعني أنهما خضراوان تضرب خضرتهما إلى السواد وكل نبت أخضر فتمام خضرته وريه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r7.claim: The earlier gardens have branching boughs or diverse pleasures, whereas these are dark green from abundant watering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r7.anchor: وقال هناك: {ذواتا أفنان} : وهي الأغصان أو الفنون في الملاذ، وقال هاهنا: {مدهامتان} أي سوداوان من شدة الري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens have darkened from greenness because they received plentiful water; elsewhere he glosses the word simply as green.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: {مدهامتان} قد اسودتا من الخضرة، من شدة الري من الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, glosses the gardens as green; similar glosses are transmitted from Abu Ayyub, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Abi Awfa, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid in one report, ʿAta, ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafiʿ, and Sufyan al-Thawri.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the gardens are filled with greenness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r10.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: {مدهامتان} : ممتلئتان من الخضرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r11.claim: Qatada says they are green from abundant watering and luxuriant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: خضراوان من الري ناعمتان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r12.claim: The freshness follows from branches luxuriantly verdant and interwoven with one another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r12.anchor: ولا شك في نضارة الأغصان على الأشجار المشبكة بعضها في بعض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r13.claim: The first pair has two flowing springs, while the second has two gushing springs; flowing is stronger than gushing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p506/r13.anchor: أي فياضتان. والجري أقوى من النضخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.claim: Mudhāmmatān means the gardens are intensely green.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens are green.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r7.anchor: أحدها : أي خضراوان , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r8.claim: Mujahid says they are black, deriving the term from al-dahma, blackness; dark horses are likewise called adham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r8.anchor: مسودتان , قاله مجاهد , مأخوذ من الدهمة وهي السواد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r9.claim: Qatada describes the gardens as verdant and lush.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p440/r9.anchor: [ خضروان من الري ] ناعمتان , قاله قتادة

MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r1.claim: Mujahid describes the two gardens as dark from abundant watering, that is, lush and deep green.
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾ يعني سوداوان من الري

MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr instead glosses the two gardens as green; the source gives both explanations without stating a preference.
MUJAHID:v2p643#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال يعني خضراوين

MUQATIL:55:56-69/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:56-69/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:56-69/r9.claim: The two gardens are dark from their abundant water and greenery.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p205#7/r1.claim: The two gardens are black-green from the intensity of their greenness.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:62-64/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:62-64/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:62-64/r14.claim: The first gardens have abundant branches, while the later pair is described by deep green color alone; further differences may remain unmentioned.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:62-64/r14.anchor: وقال في الأوليين: { ذواتآ أفنان } وفي الأخريين { مدهامتان }

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain the gardens as green because of abundant water.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r2.anchor: أي خضراوان من الري قاله ابن عباس وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r3.claim: Mujahid says the gardens are blackened or very dark.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r4.claim: Dahma means black; the verse describes gardens made black by extreme greenness and wetness, since Arabs call green things black.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r4.anchor: أي سوداوان من شدة الخضرة من الري والعرب تقول لكل أخضر أسود.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r5.claim: The author gives dark horses and camels as examples of adham, distinguishes a still blacker color as jaww, and explains idhimām as becoming black.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r5.anchor: والدهمة في اللغة السواد يقال: فرس أدهم وبعير أدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r6.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r6.claim: Labid’s line describes green or dark troops in a woven covering; the commentary identifies al-sannūr as armor-like clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r6.anchor:
وقال لبيد يرثي قتلى هوازن:
وجاؤوا به في هودج ووراءه
كتائب خضر

QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r7.claim: The author notes Iraq’s villages are called Sawād for their greenness, night is called green, and their greenery can mean a people’s multitude.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:64/r7.anchor: وسميت قرى العراق سوادا لكثرة خضرتها. ويقال لليل المظلم: أخضر.

QASHANI:55:60-66/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:60-66/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:60-66/r5.claim: The two gardens are at the utmost degree of joy, beauty, and freshness.

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes below them as lower in rank, citing contrasts between these gardens and the first pair in foliage, fountains, fruit, and furnishings.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r2.anchor: وهو ما اختاره صاحب الكشاف وقال قوله : { مدهامتان } مع قوله

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r6.claim: The gardens are intensely green; idhām normally means turning black, but very deep greenery takes on a blackish cast.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r6.anchor: أي مخضرتان في غاية الخضرة ، وإدهام الشيء أي اسواد لكن لا يستعمل في بعض الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r7.claim: He argues that whiteness is the beginning of colors and blackness their end: white accepts every color, whereas black accepts none.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r7.anchor: التحقيق فيه أن ابتداء الألوان هو البياض

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r8.claim: The Prophet's saying about adhering to the great majority and belonging to the people whose ranks one joins illustrates the use of sawād for a large community.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r8.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( عليكم بالسواد الأعظم

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r9.claim: He adds that the term kāfir is applied to black, not other colors, as part of his account of blackness as the terminal color.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r9.anchor: ولهذا يطلق الكافر على الأسود ولا يطلق على لون آخر

RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r10.claim: Bare land is called white land and cultivated land black land; this supports the lower gardens' position beneath the first pair, with branches overhead and green ground below.
RAZI-FULL:v29p116#2/r10.anchor: ولما كانت الخالية عن الزرع متصفة بالبياض واللاخالية بالسواد فهذا يدل على أنهما تحت الأوليين مكانا

STUDYQURAN:55:64/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r1.claim: Mudhāmmatān means a very dark green, caused by dense vegetation.
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r1.anchor: Deepest green ( mudhāmmatān ) indicates a very dark shade of green due to the density of vegetation

STUDYQURAN:55:64/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r2.claim: Some take the phrase to mean the Gardens’ ground is thickly vegetated, unlike the first two Gardens, where trees predominate and branches abound in green (55:48).
STUDYQURAN:55:64/r2.anchor: This is taken by some to indicate that the ground of these two Gardens is covered with thick vegetation

TABATABAI:55:56-74/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:56-74/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:56-74/r10.claim: The word describes intense greenness, so deep that it tends toward black; it conveys a tree’s luxuriance.
TABATABAI:55:56-74/r10.anchor: الادهمام من الدهمة اشتداد الخضرة بحيث تضرب إلى السواد وهو ابتهاج الشجرة

TABRISI:55:64-66/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:64-66/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:64-66/r6.claim: The two gardens are deep green, darkened by abundant moisture; full green tends toward black, its most beautiful state.
TABRISI:55:64-66/r6.anchor: أي من خضرتهما قد اسودتا من الري وكل نبت أخضر فتمام خضرته أن يضرب إلى السواد

TABRISI:55:64-66/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:64-66/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:55:64-66/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the four gardens as all belonging to those who fear their Lord's station.
TABRISI:55:64-66/r7.anchor: وهذا على قول من قال إن الجنات الأربع لمن خاف مقام ربه وهو قول ابن عباس

TABRISI:55:64-66/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:64-66/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:55:64-66/r8.claim: Hasan assigns the first two gardens to the forerunners and the latter two to their followers.
TABRISI:55:64-66/r8.anchor: وقيل: الأوليان للسابقين والأخريان للتابعين عن الحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says the gardens are so green that lushness makes them appear black.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: من خضرتهما قد اسودتا من الري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq says any green plant at the height of its greenness and freshness tends toward black.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وكل نبت اخضر، فتمام خضرته وريه أن يضرب إلى السواد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r3.claim: Dahmah means blackness; al-Layth says a crop has idhāmm when its lushness has made it dark.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r3.anchor: وقال الليث: ادهام الزرع إذا علاه السواد ريا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the gardens as intensely green, tending toward black.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شديد الخضرة إلى السواد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi likewise describes them as green with blackness from the intensity of their greenery and lushness; intense green tends toward black.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: خضراوان قد علاهما سواد من شدة الخضرة والري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r6.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says Arabs call green black; al-Qutami's verse describes the dark of night as green.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: الخضرة عند العرب سواد، وأنشد القطامي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r7.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r7.claim: Dhu al-Rumma also calls the shadow green in a line about an owl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r7.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: في ظل أخضر يدعو هامة البوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r8.claim: The expression May God destroy their khadrāʾ means their blackness or abundance, using green as black.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r8.anchor: ومن هذا يقال أباد الله خضراءهم أي سوادهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r9.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r9.claim: Dhu al-Rumma describes rain-covered vegetation as Abyssinian because its greenness has grown intense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r9.anchor: فهو قول ذي الرمة أنشده ابن قتيبة في تفسير هذه الآية يصف غيثا:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r10.claim: The following cited line describes a garden with intense greenness, calling it ḥawāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r10.anchor: وكذلك قوله أيضا أنشد أبو علي في تفسير هذه الآية:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r11.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r11.claim: Abu Ali notes the reverse usage: drought is described as white; Aws's line says barren years gleam because they have no fertility or vegetation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p193#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي: وعلى ضد هذا وصف الجدب البياض فقيل سنة شهداء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p442/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p442/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p442/r1.claim: Mudhāmmatān means intensely dark green from the richness of the greenery and moisture; Dhu al-Rumma's poetic word ḥabashiyya illustrates that deep green.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p442/r1.anchor: قال ذو الرمة -وذكر غيثا-: كسا الأكم بهمى غضة حبشية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:62-64/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:62-64/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:62-64/r2.claim: The gardens are black or dark because of the intensity of their greenery.

ELMALILI:55:56-75/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:56-75/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:56-75/r2.claim: Elmalılı renders the gardens as intensely dark green, calling them lush and verdant.

ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r11.claim: Mudhāmmatān is a feminine dual participial form from the intensive verb of darkening; from duhma, it evokes night-darkness or a dark bay horse and here denotes deep, almost black green.
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r11.anchor: Aslı “dühme”den gelir ki gece karaltısı veya

ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r12.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Ata and others gloss mudhāmmatān as khadrāwān, green.
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r12.anchor: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, İbn Cübeyr, İkrime, Atâ, İbn Ebî Rebâh ve daha sâirleri “hadrâvân” diye tefsir etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r13.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r13.claim: Abu Ayyub asked the Prophet about the phrase, and the Prophet explained it as green.
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r13.anchor: kavl-i ilâhîsinden sordum, Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm ‘hadrâvân’ buyurdu.

ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r14.claim: The description emphasizes the intensity of the gardens' greenery, like Turkish yemyeşil or gömgök.
ELMALILI:55:56-75#2/r14.anchor: Demek ki murad yeşilliklerinin kuvvetini beyandır. Lisânımızda “yemyeşil” yahut “gömgök” tâbir ederiz.

MAJAZ:v2p246/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p246/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p246/r1.claim: The two gardens are so lushly green that they have turned nearly black.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r1.claim: The Qur’an uses āya in each of the previously discussed senses, all of which are gradations of the notion of an evident sign.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r2.claim: In its most specific legal-religious usage, an āya is a Qur’anic section separated by a pause marker and forming a complete unit in the Qur’an’s arrangement.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r2.anchor: Kur’ân’ın harflerinden bir fâsıla ile ayrılmış olan zümrelerinden her birine bir âyet denilir ki bunlar Kur’ân’ın nazmında birer cüz’-i tâm teşkîl ederler.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r3.claim: Most verses are independent statements of one or several sentences, but some are only a distinct single or compound qualifier; al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm in al-Fātiḥa are one verse comprising two attributes, not a sentence.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r3.anchor: Âyetlerin ekserîsi bir veya birkaç cümleden müteşekkil müstakil birer kelâmdırlar. Ma‘amâfîh içlerinde bir cümle teşkil etmeyen müfred veya mürekkeb mümtaz birer sıfat gibi kayıt hâlinde bulunanlar da vardır.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r4.claim: Mudhāmmatān is a single word, yet it can be recited independently with the force of a complete utterance and paused upon.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r4.anchor: bir kelimedir, böyle iken bunlar bir kelâm neş’esiyle

ELMALILI:v1p108/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r5.claim: In al-Muddaththir, thumma naẓara is two words forming one sentence, while thumma ʿabasa wa-basara is four words forming two sentences.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r5.anchor: Müddessir sûresinde ثُمَّ نَظَرَ [el-Müddessir 74/21][^6] iki kelime bir cümledir.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r6.claim: Verses have short, medium, and long forms; examples range from about half a page for Āyat al-Kursī and the ablution verse to a full page for Āyat al-Mudāyana.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r6.anchor: Bu suretle âyetlerin kısası, ortası, uzunu ve her birinin mütenevvi‘mertebeleri vardır.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r7.claim: Verse-final letters (fawāṣil) are not always uniform; they vary through patterns that may or may not be specific.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r7.anchor: Fâsıla harfleri de dâima muttarid değil, gâh mahsus, gâh gayr-i mahsus farklarla tenevvü‘eder.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r8.claim: Because verse forms and endings vary, the separation and ordering of verses are tawqīfī: they depend on transmitted reports and cannot be determined by reason alone as poetic lines or sajʿ units can.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r8.anchor: âyetlerin ayrılması ve tertîbi tevkīfîdir. Yani şiirin mısrâ‘ı, seci‘in fıkrası gibi yalnız dirayet ile tâyin olunamaz, rivayete mütevakkıf olur.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r9.claim: Reason alone cannot establish that Ḥā-Mīm and ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf comprise two verses; their verse division is known through transmission.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r9.anchor: حٰمٓ. عٓسٓقٓ iki âyet olduğu yalnız dirayet ile bilinemez.

ELMALILI:v1p108/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p108/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p108/r10.claim: By extension, any Qur’anic section that expresses a divine ruling is also called an āya.
ELMALILI:v1p108/r10.anchor: Daha sonra Kur’ân’ın ahkâm-ı ilâhiyeden bir hüküm ifade eden her kısmına da bir âyet ıtlak

BURHAN:v1p266/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r10.speaker: ابن المنير
BURHAN:v1p266/r10.claim: Ibn al-Munīr says that “dark green” is the Qur’an’s only one-word āya.
BURHAN:v1p266/r10.anchor: وقال ابن المنير فى البحر ليس فى القرآن كلمة واحدة آية إلا ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾

BURHAN:v3p225/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p225/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p225/r7.claim: Mudhāmmatān means darkened by the intensity of their greenness.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#9/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#9/r1.claim: Afnān encompasses several kinds of blessing, making the first pair's description superior; mudhāmmatān means darkened toward black by intense greenness.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#9/r1.anchor: والوصف الأول أعلى فإن الأفنان تطلق على ضروب عدة من النعم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.claim: Verse endings are not always self-contained semantic units: meaning comes first, and a fāṣila may depend on what precedes or follows it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.anchor: ليست الفواصل هي دائماً تامة المعنى فقد تكون متعلقة بما قبلها أوما بعدها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.claim: A Qur'anic verse ending is not always a complete semantic unit: it may remain attached to what precedes or follows, as in these examples.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.anchor: الآيات ليست وحدات مستقلة المعنى قد تكون تامة وقد تكون متعلقة بما قبلها أو بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r6.claim: The shortest verse by word count is muddhamatan, while the shortest by disjoint letters is Ta Ha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r6.anchor: وأقصر آية في عدد الكلمات قوله تعالى ) مدهامتان ( . في سورة الرحمن وفي عدد الحروف المقطعة قوله ) طه (
